messages:
Maya: Quick sync — I want to propose an "ownership federation" model for long-lived infra services. TL;DR: small dedicated service owners + federated org-level guardians, explicit API fences, and a debt-waterfall cadence for paydown. Thoughts?
Sam: nice framing. can you sketch the concrete boundaries you're imagining? worried about cross-team debugging and decision friction. :thinking_face:
Maya: sketch below — this is intentionally coarse: 
```
- Service owner: full responsibility for implementation, SLA, and runtime deploys
- Federation guardians: own cross-cutting contracts, shared sidecars (auth/telemetry), and migration playbooks
- Adapters: thin shim layer per consumer to insulate changes
- Debt-waterfall: rank tech debt by customer impact -> cut into sprintable tranches
```
Liam: +1 on adapters. our past pain was direct coupling to internal helpers. thin shims make cutovers easier. how do we keep API surface minimal?
Maya: limit public API to 2-3 primitives per service where possible, move complex flows into composable helpers behind the adapter. enforce via API review and automated contract tests.
Nina: can we rely on sidecars for telemetry/observability? ops team has concerns about sidecar resource overhead.
ops-bot: FYI — recent perf tests show sidecar mem overhead ~40MB avg on p3-small. CPU negligible. Link: https://perf.redwood.internal/sidecar-overhead
Sam: oks — sidecar overhead seems manageable. still: how do we prioritize the debt-waterfall? we have a huge backlog.
Maya: propose a simple scoring function for each debt item: 
- customer_impact: 0-5
- failure_rate_delta: 0-5
- cost_savings_estimate: 0-5
- ease_of_fix: 0-5
Total score -> buckets (critical / high / medium / low). Wire into triage board and dedicate one sprint per quarter to top N items.
Liam: sounds reasonable. also recommend a "safety adapter" pattern for high-risk changes: keep an emergency fallback adapter that can be toggled per-tenant while we iterate.
Maya: yes — toggle + canary rollout policy at traffic-router level. We'll expose a flag in the router policy to route X% to new owner.
Nina: what about migration toolchain? extracting stateful pieces is risky. we need a checklist.
Maya: suggested migration checklist (short): 
1) define API contract and schema migration plan
2) add adapter shim in front of old service (non-breaking)
3) mirror-write to new service for a week, run discrepancy checks
4) enable canary traffic -> ramp based on error/latency thresholds
5) cutover and prune shim after 2 stable weeks

Sam: will the federation guardians be a formal team or a role rotation?
Maya: prefer a 6-mo role rotation initially (2 senior engs from each org), later formalize into a platform governance council if load justifies it.
Liam: one operational concern: ownership proliferation. we should define "ownership granularity" guardrails (max X services per owner).
Maya: agreed — propose: no owner should have more than 5 runtime services; otherwise we assign a co-owner. helps avoid knowledge silos.
Nina: how do we measure progress on debt-paydown? metrics?
Maya: track: number of critical debt items closed, mean time to rollback for migrations, API compatibility regressions (0 target), and cost delta from quantized pieces. Dashboards in Console + weekly triage notes.
Sam: ok. concrete asks from me: 1) list of candidate services for 1st wave, 2) draft adapter template, 3) canary policy knobs. i can own #2 and #3.
Maya: awesome — I'll assemble candidate list by EOD Friday. Liam, can you pair with Sam on adapter template?
Liam: happy to. suggest we include a small integration test harness in the template (request/response fuzz + contract assertions).
ops-bot: note created: #ownership-federation epic (link: https://boards.redwood.internal/epics/1234). Maya added 3 tasks.
Nina: last comment — we should reserve a "debt safety budget" in sprint planning so teams can opt-in without killing feature velocity. even 10% capacity helps.
Maya: totally. propose adding a sprint-level checkbox for teams to allocate at least 8-12% capacity for proven debt items during the pilot.
Sam: cool. I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with the scoring rubric and migration checklist. ping me for reviews. :rocket:
Maya: thanks all — this was useful. we'll iterate on the RFC doc and surface to platform council in two weeks.
